topic: Inertia and Newton's first law of motion
key_concepts: Inertia is an object's inherent resistance to changes in its state of motion
An object at rest remains at rest unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
A moving object continues moving at constant velocity in a straight line unless acted on b
No force is required to keep an object moving at constant velocity
Friction is a force that opposes sliding between surfaces
Friction can also enable motion, such as when walking
Frictional force depends on the type of surfaces in contact
Static friction acts between surfaces at rest and is greater than kinetic friction
Galileo reasoned that an object would move indefinitely in the absence of friction
A net force changes an object's state of motion or acceleration
Centripetal force keeps an object moving in a circular path
Removing centripetal force allows an object to move in a straight line at constant speed
